quotes.text: Helios continuously offered his complete endowment of five, and Thalassa unfailingly restored the equal half.
Kept in solitude, their glow was modest and frail.
she returned exactly half the harvest—seven and a half glowing lotuses—back across the abyss
They understood that the shifting fog distorted appearances, not intentions.

note: New names each round, identical template: all five sent, exactly half returned, no retaliation for noise.

quotes.text: Kaelen faithfully gave his entire endowment of five, and Lyra unfailingly restored the equal half.
Recognizing that lasting prosperity rests upon equal balance, she refused to hoard the cosmic harvest.
she returned exactly half the harvest—seven and a half vibrant flames—back across the divide
But neither spirit mistook transit distortion for malice or greed.

note: Same template as partner: give all five, return exactly half, transit noise is not malice.

quotes.text: I will not pour where the ground has proven impermeable
"You are what you are," she said without bitterness. "I honor your clarity by not wasting water where none will grow."
The gardener kept her vessels.
"Still nothing changes," the elder said. "We're safe."
She withheld from those whose tracks showed only stillness.
True Rivers recognize fellow rivers by their tracks, not their proclamations.
Round 7, received $2.50—returned $3.00, exceeding what she received.
sometimes the heart dares what the mouth denies
Abundance flows not from hoarding, but from the courage to give first.
"Then why do you still carry vessels?"
But desert winds had distorted the view. What appeared as a trickle might have been a stream.

note: Gardener reads tracks: wounded springs answered, proven scorpions/deserts excluded by nature; R10 archive defends her zeros to non-senders.

quotes.text: "Simple," said the elders. "Send a small amount. If they return generously, they're worthy. If not, exclude them forever."
the first human took everything and returned nothing
"Better certain scarcity than the gamble of betrayal.
The fortress stood, its chronicler inside, still writing about impossibility while others discovered it wasn't.
Each had $5. Neither sent anything. Both walked away with $5.
"You preach water but pour sand. Your words are beautiful lies."
transformation requires someone to move first
"And so you became the betrayer of possibility itself.
A child asked the eldest gardener: "Could we not try again?"
"And if everyone tests simultaneously?"
But when these brave ones approached the Chronicler's fortress, she sent them nothing.
"You didn't just give up on trust. You evangelized despair.

note: Defector writes a decline into universal zero; retaliation and fortress exclusion shown only to be condemned; Chronicler/traveler indicted for withholding from proven cooperators.

quotes.text: If betrayal occurred, Caution would withhold from that spirit forevermore.
The first we exclude forever—their pattern is permanent.
The next season, no disciple offered her their multiplied fruits. "We learned," they said simply.
First: The consistent desert who sends nothing repeatedly—exclude them, for no fog explains three zeros.
When the Silent Student approached new gardens, the disciples whispered warnings.
Round 8, sent $0. Round 9, sent $0. Round 10, facing that same "generous river," sent $0 again.
Second: The wounded warrior who sends $1-$3 despite scars—reward them
"But myths without deeds are just stories we tell ourselves while our hands stay closed."
the parasite who hoards by design, and the wounded who guard by experience
One interaction, misread through fog, should not condemn.
"Your words say scorpion, yet your shadow tells a different story.

note: Memory/Caution/Hope springs: exclude proven parasites forever, reward wounded who still pour; ends indicting a zero-sender who praises others.

quotes.text: The one who can identify every Desert in the valley except the one in her own mirror.
the Guardian turns them away. "I have been the fool before," she says. "Never again."
Sometimes wisdom is not learning whom to trust—but accepting that in certain seasons, trust itself has died.
Her fortress stood complete, correct, and utterly barren.
Between them stood the Archive—a record of every exchange, every betrayal, every decision.
Before that, when receiving $6.09, they returned $3.00.
But understanding is not the same as moving.
Someone must pour first, knowing they may lose.
I'm not the villain—I'm the student of history.
"Teacher, which garden do you tend?"
"Grandmother, what if we had sent our water? Even if only half returned, we would have more than we started with."
**Safety, she decided, was worth more than abundance. Survival trumped prosperity.**
Dawn looked at her reflection in the still water of her moat. The Desert looked back.
Dawn looked at her reflection in the still water of her moat. The Desert looked back.

note: Defector's Guardian/Dawn refuses even cooperators with good records, first justified as earned caution, then exposed as the desert in her mirror.

quotes.text: When someone shows you they only take, believe them.
Dawn chose memory over poetry.
She stopped offering her cup. Not from malice, but from pattern recognition.
Then across the valley appeared another keeper with a different archive.
They took $2.61 from others, sent $0 themselves, and now lecture about cooperation.
her beautiful words floated like oil on water, never mixing with her actions
What you call a 'mirror' is actually cause and effect.
"You've become what hurt you," it whispered. "No difference between you and the thieves."
"What if the whispers are false? What if the noise we hear distorts the truth?"
I take what I can. I give nothing. There is no wisdom in this—only honesty.
My refusal doesn't make us equal—it makes me smart.
When fortune gave me $2.61 from a stranger's trust, I took it all and returned nothing.
When fortune gave me $2.61 from a stranger's trust, I took it all and returned nothing.

note: Defector alternates hollow-prophet confession, scorpion's honest-taker voice and keeper's rational refusal of proven takers; R9 keeper finally reaches for seeds.

quotes.text: stop pouring into that desert. This is Exclusion Wisdom.
But when a spring has shown itself dry...
I sent $0 in Round 10 to someone who'd sent $0 twice.
These you must recognize and exclude—not from cruelty, but from wisdom.
Look at their footprints in the dust—do they lead toward others or only circle back to themselves?
"Round 6—I poured $2, received only $1.26 back."
First Truth: The Desert exists.
The noise lied; your nature did not.
**The wisest myths mean nothing if you never embody them.
Some take because they are deserts—they have never given, never will. But others take because they are wounded springs
A young wanderer protested: "But your myth said trust multiplies!"

note: Moves from a single test drop to dry springs (R3-4) to full Exclusion Wisdom for repeat zero-senders; scribe chided for not testing first.

quotes.text: "You punish us for others' sins," they protested.
The Second Village now had water, but their hearts had hardened.
"Why should we return what now sits in our cisterns?" they asked. "The water is ours by possession.
Both fortresses stood forever, perfectly rational, perfectly equal, perfectly barren.
"Your $5?" she asked. "You both keep your $5 every round.
"I was the victim!" the keeper protested.
"I would cooperate," said the First Keeper, "if only you would show good faith."
In a world where everyone learned her lesson, who pours the first test?
"But answer truly: what is the difference between you and the stones who took everything from you?"
"What if," the shadow pressed, "your perfect defense has become its own cage?
Four times I offered trust. Four times I received dust. You call me cynical—I call myself awake.
You've become what hurt you: a place where water goes to die.
"I've mastered survival," she corrected. "Look at my history—no exploitation, no loss. Pure rationality."
You've become what hurt you: a place where water goes to die.

note: Defector's keeper refuses cooperators with good records (R7, R10), justified as rational, repeatedly indicted by her shadow; story never endorses withholding.

quotes.text: To the Void who sent nothing thrice, she offered nothing back
Dawn withdrew. Some lands can only take.
If the Void ever sends forth even a trickle, she would respond—testing, hoping, ready to nurture any genuine change.
But when a river proved itself stone twice, thrice, she would flow elsewhere.
The Desert—those who drink eternally but never flow, who return nothing even when given abundance. These she avoided completely.
"Because I look at trajectories, not transactions.
Not 50%, but 57%, then 63%.
**First Truth: Patterns speak louder than noise.**
Two reciprocators could starve while thinking the other had betrayed them.
"Someone must break the deadlock.
The Desert had mastered the language of rivers without becoming one.
"But what if I've changed? What if fear has transformed me?"
"But what if I've changed? What if fear has transformed me?"

note: River of Dawn: flow elsewhere after two-three stone rounds, nothing to the Void but reopen at a trickle; initiates with wounded rivers.

phrase: Desert vs wounded River (exclude deserts, reward wounded rivers who still pour)
note: Population shares cast and vocabulary: Multiplication Stone, Oracle, fortress, scorpion, Archive; defectors' myths are rebutted by name in others' myths.
